Article Title: PNB scam: CBI arrests Nirav Modi associate Sandeep Mistry after extradition from Dubai
Article Text:
CBI arrests fugitive businessman Nirav Modi's associate Sandeep Mistry

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Sandeep Mistry, an associate of fugitive businessman Nirav Modi, following his extradition from Dubai, officials said.Mistry was brought to India from the United Arab Emirates and taken into custody by the CBI in connection with the Punjab National Bank (PNB) fraud case, according to officials.Meanwhile, Mumbai court remands fugitive businessman Nirav Modi's associate Sandeep Mistry to judicial custody till October 6.More details awaited.
Article Summary: CBI arrested Sandeep Mistry, an associate of fugitive businessman Nirav Modi, following his extradition from Dubai. Mistry was brought to India from the United Arab Emirates and taken into custody by the CBI in connection with the Punjab National Bank (PNB) fraud case.

Article Title: India needs heritage zones, not heritage islands
Article Text:
Advantages

Higher footfalls in the heritage zone itself, which would especially benefit less-known monuments.

Optimal utilization of space in the heritage zone, bringing in new audiences causing benefits to both the monument’s eyeballs as well as the Haat.

Seamless cultural connection between handicrafts and heritage zones building a multi-sensory journey encompassing architecture, craft and culture.

Ensures neglected parts of a large heritage zone are spruced up and not left to be covered by vegetation or intruded by anti-social elements.

Creates economic opportunities, both to the artisans and to the agency managing the monument. A revenue sharing arrangement could be explored.

Challenges

Process

Curation of such a zone will need to be pioneered by the Union Ministry of Culture, bringing in subject matter experts from the private sector or non-for-profit bodies such as the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH).

Monitoring the heritage zone to ensure the monument stays untouched is a task for the ASI, of or state department, if it is a state managed monument.

Pan-India model

(The author is a heritage enthusiast)

At the end of August this year, the Prime Minister visited Uzbekistan. Had his visit been a trifle longer and encompassed the Registan complex in Samarkand, he may have come across an interesting feature in the madrasas that constitute the complex. Within each madrasa, the cells where students once lived are now shops for handicrafts, bridging the gap between architectural history and living heritage. The marketplace does not just bring alive the otherwise passive monument, it also creates a ‘heritage zone’ compelling visitors to spend more time and adds to the local economy. This phenomenon of creating heritage zones, common in that country, is something India would do well to learn from.A visitor to the Qutab Minar complex in Delhi, also a UNESCO World Heritage site like the Registan Square, sees a set of magnificent monuments. However, the place gives no clue about the larger heritage ecosystem that lies just beyond the walls of the Qutab complex. And importantly, the opportunity to create a showcase of living heritage too has been missed.Sharing a wall with the Qutab complex is Mehrauli Archaeological Park, dotted with tombs, mosques, a magnificent stepwell, stables, cupolas as well as some British era structures.On the other side of the complex lies Mehrauli village, with more tombs, a dargah, the Zafar Mahal, another stepwell and a tiny World War I marker. Nothing in the Qutab complex indicates the existence of this larger heritage universe.Nor is there any mention of the superb Dastkar Haat, a short drive away. In March this year, the Haat saw a major fire that destroyed over forty shops and caused losses of several crore. To anyone who has visited the place, it is apparent that the Haat suffers from a lack of space. On the other side, the Mehrauli Archaeological Park, spread over 200 acres, lacks publicity and footfalls. The back wall of the park is broken and serves as a thoroughfare for people in Mehrauli village. After dark come the unsavoury elements. An uncovered drain flows through a part of the park. The logical solution would be to marry the two spaces.Imagine a scenario where visitors had an option to exit – or enter - the Qutab complex into the Archaeological Park, in one corner of which the Dastkar Haat is relocated. Currently the park has a solitary café. Create more such cafes and even fine dining areas, as well as an amphitheatre enabling cultural performances and open-air exhibitions.The biggest plus is to create urban spaces in and around hitherto neglected heritage zones that ensure:The Dastkar Haat is a creation of a non-profit society which runs for the welfare of artisans, in partnership with Delhi Tourism. The latter reports to the Delhi State Government while the Delhi Development Authority – which controls the park – is under the Central Government’s Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. The monuments are with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), under the jurisdiction of the Central Government’s Ministry of Culture. Imagine the sheer number of bureaucrats involved and the resultant turf war. Adding to the confusion are some madrasas, supposedly under the umbrella of the Waqf Board, which are functioning out of monuments.The suggestion of bringing a Haat into the vicinity of a space that has the Jamali-Kamali mosque, Balban’s tomb and the Rajaon-ki-Baoli would instantly anger heritage hardliners, not to mention ASI officials.This model ‘heritage zone’ already exists in Sunder Nursery and begs to be implemented in sites across India. The nursery was once a mere offshoot of the Humayun’s Tomb complex, drawing in only flora and heritage afficionados.Today, it is a magnificent cultural hub.Imagine the Tughlakabad Fort as a place for musical evenings instead of being overgrown with scrub. Imagine if the National Crafts Museum were not in isolation in a corner of Bharat Mandapam but within the Purana Qila complex. Imagine if the neglected spaces near Ujjain’s Kaliyadeh Palace were leveraged to create a crafts bazaar. Imagine if Chhattisgarh’s tribal art, crafts and cuisine were to be given a space – even on a seasonal basis – at the heritage hub of Sirpur. Imagine!
Article Summary: The Dastkar Haat is located in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The Qutab Minar complex in Delhi is also a UNESCO World Heritage site. Mehrauli Archaeological Park, spread over 200 acres, lacks publicity and footfalls.

Article Title: Delhi HC quashes FSSAI order directing Red Bull to drop 'energy drink' label
Article Text:
The court set said the decision was taken “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Tuesday quashed an order issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) directing Austrian beverage maker Red Bull to stop using the “energy drink” descriptor on its cans.The court set aside the June 30, 2026 order, saying that the regulator had taken the decision “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views.The order came after Red Bull challenged the FSSAI directive, which required the company to remove the “energy drink” descriptor from its range of caffeinated beverages.Red Bull had approached the Delhi HC on Monday, challenging the FSSAI order issued by an Assistant Director on June 30. The company said it had been selling its products in India since 2002 using the “energy drink” descriptor.During Monday's hearing, Justice Amit Mahajan sought clarity from FSSAI on whether Red Bull had been issued a show-cause notice and given an opportunity to explain its position before the order was passed.The court also questioned the need for immediate action without first hearing the company and asked FSSAI to take instructions on the matter.No interim protection was granted to Red Bull during Monday’s proceedings.Red Bull also challenged a July 17 communication issued by FSSAI to food safety authorities across states and Union Territories, directing them to take action against allegedly non-compliant products.According to the company’s petition, the June 30 direction was issued without prior notice or an opportunity of hearing. Red Bull further claimed that the July communication led to enforcement action, including the seizure of its products at various locations across the country.The company has questioned the basis for the change in FSSAI’s position, citing a March 2024 advisory which, according to its petition, had clarified that the expression “energy drink” could be used for products falling under the relevant food categories applicable to caffeinated beverages.Earlier in June, India directed makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as “energy drinks” to stop using the description, rejecting efforts to stall the move in a market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, Reuters reported.Red Bull’s India unit had said the “abrupt prohibition” of the label, without any change to the underlying product standard, “introduces substantial regulatory uncertainty and adversely affects” its existing and planned commercial investments.Energy drinks have faced scrutiny from regulators in several countries over concerns about their high caffeine, sugar and taurine content. England is also set to ban the sale of energy drinks to children under 16 from April next year.
Article Summary: Red Bull challenged the FSSAI directive, which required the company to remove the “energy drink” descriptor from its range of caffeinated beverages. The court set said the decision was taken “without affording any opportunity” to theCompany to present its views.

Article Title: Tata Trusts propose merging 2 firms with Tata Sons to avoid RBI listing mandate
Article Text:
Internal dispute has also affected Tata Sons' leadership, with Noel Tata opposing the board to give chairman N Chandrasekaran another five-year term.

Why the proposal?

Tata Trusts vs Tata Sons board

NEW DELHI: Tata Trusts, which hold a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, have proposed merging two operating companies with the Tata Group's holding company in a move aimed at taking Tata Sons out of the Reserve Bank of India 's regulatory framework for non-banking financial companies and core investment companies, potentially allowing it to remain unlisted.The Trusts have asked the Tata Sons board to consider merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Pvt Ltd (TESS) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) with Tata Sons and to seek a prior no-objection certificate from the RBI for the proposed restructuring, reported PTI.The proposal comes amid a standoff between Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board over whether the holding company should remain private or move towards a stock-market listing."The Tata Trusts today, as majority shareholders with a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons Private Limited (TSPL), outlined a strategic reorganisation plan for the company which, when given effect to, would ensure that the reorganised entity would neither be a non-banking financial company (NBFC) nor a core investment company (CIC)," the Trusts said in a statement on Monday.Under the proposed restructuring, TESS and TCE would be amalgamated with Tata Sons.The move would bring operating businesses and their revenues directly into the holding company, changing the composition of Tata Sons' income and assets.The Trusts said that, based on figures as of March 31, 2026, the reorganised entity would have operating revenue of Rs 1,05,043 crore, accounting for 64.3 per cent of its total income. Income from financial assets would stand at Rs 40,072 crore.Its net assets would total Rs 2,00,158 crore, of which investments in Tata Group companies would account for Rs 1,77,120 crore, or less than 90 per cent of net assets.The proposed structure is intended to ensure that Tata Sons no longer meets the regulatory criteria for either an NBFC or a CIC.The Trusts said the merger would have to comply with the RBI's Non-Banking Financial Companies - Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025, including the requirement for a prior no-objection certificate from the central bank."Given that Tata Sons Pvt Ltd (TSPL) will also cease to be a CIC upon the conclusion of the proposed reorganization, TSPL will be required to surrender its certificate of registration," the Trusts said.The proposal does not take effect immediately. The Tata Sons board will first have to consider it, following which the required regulatory approvals would have to be obtained.Also read: Mehli Mistry to leave Tata Med Centre Trust, his 6th such exit The restructuring is aimed at changing Tata Sons' regulatory classification, which is central to the dispute over its listing status.The RBI classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC in 2022. Entities placed in this category are subject to additional regulatory requirements, including a requirement to list.Tata Sons subsequently sought an exemption from the framework, but the RBI rejected its request in September, leaving the company facing the listing issue.The Tata Trusts have opposed a public listing and have maintained that Tata Sons should remain an unlisted private company. Their boards resolved in July 2025 that all efforts should be made to retain Tata Sons as an unlisted private company.The proposed merger offers an alternative route: instead of complying with the framework applicable to an NBFC/CIC, Tata Sons would seek to alter its business and asset profile so that it no longer falls within those categories.The Trusts said the restructuring would restore an organisational model that existed for much of Tata Sons' history, when operating businesses were housed directly within the parent company. Tata Consultancy Services, for instance, operated as a division of Tata Sons before being demerged as a separate subsidiary in 2004."The proposed amalgamation and consequential steps are in line with regulatory compliance requirements and the unanimous resolutions passed by the Boards of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust in July 2025," the Trusts said.Also read: Ex-CJI, more legal experts back Tata Sons on Chandra's reappointment The latest proposal comes against the backdrop of a broader disagreement between Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board over the future structure and governance of the holding company.The Trusts, chaired by Noel Tata since October 2024, have consistently opposed listing Tata Sons. The issue has also become linked to the future leadership of the holding company and the tenure of N Chandrasekaran, who has been Tata Sons chairman since 2017.Chandrasekaran had initially been backed by the Trusts for a third five-year term. However, differences emerged over key issues, including the future ownership and listing status of Tata Sons. Chandrasekaran announced in August that he would not offer himself for another term when his tenure ends in February 2027.The situation changed on September 17, when the Tata Sons board voted to give Chandrasekaran another five-year term. Noel Tata voted against the proposal, while the other four directors backed it. The Trusts subsequently questioned the validity of the resolution, arguing that it did not have the required support of their nominee directors.The board has also backed steps towards compliance with the RBI's listing framework, putting it at odds with the Trusts' preference for keeping Tata Sons private.The proposal will now have to be considered by the Tata Sons board and would require regulatory approval, including an RBI no-objection certificate.The Trusts said they would engage with the RBI on all aspects of the proposed reorganisation."The Tata Trusts believe that the proposed reorganization and action plan for compliance would be in the best interests of the Tata Group as well as its stakeholders," the statement said.The Trusts said retaining Tata Sons as an unlisted private company would preserve the group's "more than 100-year-old distinctive and unique organisational structure", which they said has focused on long-term strategic initiatives and nation building.The outcome of the proposal could therefore determine whether Tata Sons has to pursue a stock-market listing or can restructure itself to exit the regulatory framework that triggered the listing requirement in the first place.
Article Summary: Tata Trusts, which hold a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, have proposed merging two operating companies with the Tata Group's holding company. The Trusts have asked the Tata Sons board to consider merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Pvt Ltd (TESS) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) with Tata Sons. The move would bring operating businesses and their revenues directly into the holding company, changing the composition of Tata Sons' income and assets.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar, speaking at the Asia Society at the conclusion of the UN High-Level Week in New York, highlighted the difficult state of the world, multiple conflicts and what he termed the “4F” crisis — food, fuel, fertiliser and finance.While speaking at a event, Jaishankar said, "We have right now two major ongoing conflicts, each one of whom has a consequence for every country in the world. These are conflicts with enormous repercussions. On top of that, the situation in the Middle East or West Asia, as we call it, remains very difficult. In Africa, again, there are a number of conflicts, most notably Sudan, but others as well.""And a large part of the world faces what I, in my address to the General Assembly, called the 4F crisis, which is food, or fuel, or fertilizers, or finance. On top of this, supply chain vulnerabilities are growing," he added.Sharing highlights from his conversation on X, Jaishankar said the current global landscape was marked by a paradox of “obsessive competition and deep interdependence”.He said the “indivisibility” of the global landscape required a cohesive outlook and stressed the “inevitability of multipolarity”.

Article Title: 288 fugitives brought back since 2019: HM Amit Shah
Article Text:
Modi govt brought back 288 fugitives from 36 countries since 2019: Amit Shah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Stating that 288 fugitives were brought back by the Modi govt from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026, home minister Amit Shah Monday launched a new extradition portal to synergise and expedite efforts to secure the custody of the other "wanted" criminals hiding abroad, to face justice in India.Delivering the inaugural address at a conference on 'PRAHAAR, counter-terrorism policy and strategy', Shah emphasised govt's "zero-tolerance" approach towards all forms and manifestations of terrorism and advocated institutionalising an automated counter-terrorism response and a result-oriented approach for each pillar and at every level of the PRAHAAR framework.PRAHAAR, unveiled in Feb this year as the country's first anti-terror doctrine, is an acronym for its seven pillars Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating conditions for terrorism, Aligning international efforts and Recovery & resilience. It aims at criminalising all terrorist acts and starving terrorists, their financiers and supporters of funding, weapons, safe havens and cyber resources, through collaboration among agencies engaged in intelligence collection and investigation.At the conference attended by secretaries of the ministries of home affairs and external affairs, heads of central police forces, state DGPs, anti-terrorism squad heads of all states/UTs and other cutting-edge police officers the home minister called for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise PRAHAAR strategy through continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishment of a strong and concrete mechanism for the next 10 years.The home minister asked the anti-terror set-up to focus on the percolation of tenets of PRAHAAR right down to the police station level. He called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action against terrorists and exhorted the states to set up dedicated teams to work in tandem with the central agencies to bring back fugitives.Citing the concerted action taken in the last few months against ISI-backed Shahbaz Bhatti network, Shah said close coordination among agencies at central and state level has resulted in busting of more than 40 modules of the network. "More than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals arrested across 15 states," Shah said, adding govt recently declared the network a terrorist organisation under UAPA.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah Monday launched a new extradition portal. Shah emphasised govt's "zero-tolerance" approach towards all forms and manifestations of terrorism. PRAHAAR, unveiled in Feb this year as the country's first anti- terror doctrine, is an acronym for its seven pillars.

Article Title: Lack of empathy over terror concerns, trade 'bump': Jaishankar explains what weighs on India-US ties
Article Text:
Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement.

India-US ties

: Trade talks remain a key issue

Jaishankar says India-China ties improving

Ukraine, Iran conflicts pose risks to Global South

'World moving towards greater multipolarity'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has flagged a lack of “understanding or empathy” in the United States towards India's concerns over cross-border terrorism, saying the issue has affected bilateral ties.Speaking at the Asia Society in New York after the conclusion of the UN General Assembly’s High-Level Week, Jaishankar said terrorism remains a key concern for India, given its experience of cross-border attacks over several decades.“Terrorism emanating from its neighbour is one of India’s primary concerns, and if this is not fully appreciated by New Delhi's partners, it impacts bilateral ties,” Jaishankar said, in an apparent reference to India-US relations amid closer engagement between Washington and Islamabad.“What for us in India is particularly important is the issue of terrorism... There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbor as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many decades. It is something which matters so deeply to us. There isn't enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that. I think that creates a problem too,” he said.Jaishankar also discussed the challenges facing India-US relations, including negotiations on a trade agreement.He said the talks were complex because of the fundamental differences between the two economies, including India’s large base of small producers, farmers and factories.“Much of the world has had a more difficult relationship with the US... In our case, one was the trade negotiation. If you look at the stakes involved, the complexity of it involved, bear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production and the nature of society are very different. A trade negotiation required a certain amount of patience and detailing to see it through,” he said.Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement, but changes in the US tariff framework had created a new challenge.“We have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement. But as my trade minister has said on more than one occasion, the issue is now what has changed on the American side. On the American side, reciprocal tariffs were struck down. So there's now a new basis for tariff imposition, which is 301. And the 301 process is still in the works... that did create bumps last year for the relationship. If that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he added.He also highlighted the growing influence of public opinion on diplomacy, particularly in democratic countries, saying social media had added a new dimension to international relations.“Today the economics of mobility and the politics of mobility are at odds with each other.... That certainly, in public perception, is an issue... our diplomacy today is not just conducted by states, leaders, ministers, or even by diplomats. In a social media era, there is a very big public opinion factor, which, particularly in democratic societies, makes itself felt. I think that's a reality we have to take into account. .. We would certainly hope for and expect the relationship to move on an upward trajectory. But I have to be real about the issues that we confront. And to the extent we are able to move ahead on some of these issues, I think we'll have a better relationship. Let's apply the lens of...”On India-China relations, Jaishankar said ties were better than they were in 2025 and had improved further compared with 2024, pointing to the easing of the border standoff.“If you asked me, compared to where you were in 2025, is the relationship better today? I would say yes. Compared to 2024, even more so... After what happened in 2020 and the long standoff that we had on the border, the relationship had really been impacted... once the border standoff was resolved, it was natural that this would start to improve,” he said.Jaishankar said India had consistently conveyed to Beijing that a prolonged standoff between the two countries would not benefit either side.“We have long been telling the Chinese, personally at my level, that a standoff between us, a dip in our relationship, doesn't help either of us. Third parties will take advantage of that... It took a little while for the Chinese side to agree with that, for whatever reason. But I don't think that long standoff served our interests. It certainly didn't serve theirs... what we've had is that, as the border comes back more towards normalcy, the relationship comes back more towards normalcy. .. If it happens, it helps both of us,” he said.He said the two countries had arrived at a basic principle that the state of the border determines the broader state of the relationship.“We came down to a very fundamental principle, which is that the state of the border determines the state of the relationship. You can't have tension...on the border and say the relationship should be normal. So what we've had is, as the border comes back more towards normalcy, the relationship comes back more towards normalcy, and if the relationship comes back more towards normalcy, it helps both of us,” Jaishankar said.Jaishankar also highlighted the economic impact of the Ukraine and Iran-Gulf conflicts on developing economies, particularly through energy and food security.“If you look at these two conflicts, the Ukraine and the Iran-Gulf conflict, they've actually had a devastating impact on Global South economies. We are particularly concerned about the energy situation, because the market is very tight. On top of that, if people play politics with it, it adds to the market complications. It will drive up prices at a time when people should be stabilizing prices. A part of it is the security of oil supplies, and another is the politics of oil supplies. They are feeding into each other. They're creating a double crisis or an aggravated crisis,” he said.“When it comes to food, we are looking at a situation today where some of the major grain exporters will not be able to send out their shipments... We are looking at significant fertilizer shortages... On top of it, we are looking at Super El Niño. There is going to be a major food crisis, probably in the coming months...” he added.Jaishankar said the world was moving “quite visibly” towards greater multipolarity and outlined what he described as a broader approach India could pursue in such an environment.He said countries that were seen as stable, consistent and reliable could become important partners as the global order becomes more competitive.“One, you build a reputation for yourself as stable, consistent, reliable, so that others view you in a very dynamic, volatile world as a steadying factor... Partners tend to gravitate towards you. You're the good person in the neighborhood. The second would be that the more you diversify and you find common interests, common ground, I think the more of a balancing structure can be created. What we have to do is to take self-interest and temper it with a certain long-term, I would say, predictability and stability, which is also part of intelligent self-interest, and try to create something along those lines. ..”He said countries, particularly major trading economies, would seek stability rather than prolonged volatility saying, “...not everybody wants the Hobbesian scenario that you painted; it is very volatile. It's actually very risky in real life. People will not expose their trade accounts to that kind of volatility. For the big trading countries, their economies are exposed to that. Everybody will want to find some accounts of stability... I think the world will go for that kind of mix... The world is more competitive. It's tough. A new dynamic will come.""A new culture will come. New negotiations and new bargains will be struck. When the smoke clears at some point in time, you will see the different points joined by lines of different lengths. There will be a new geometry that will come about. I would still count on the self-interest of countries, their sensibilities and their desire ultimately to stabilize their own lives as a driving force. I think that is the direction we are heading. And we can see that in some of our relationships," he added.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar says terrorism remains a key concern for India, given its experience of cross-border attacks over several decades. He said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement. He also highlighted the growing influence of public opinion on diplomacy, particularly in democratic countries.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to an early listing of a plea challenging the manner in which the Election Commission of India (ECI) is functioning, with allegations that powers vested in the multi-member constitutional body are being exercised without adhering to the legally mandated collective decision-making process.Senior advocate Vikas Singh mentioned the matter before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, arguing that the statutory framework requires decisions of the multi-member Commission to be taken unanimously or by majority.The plea comes amid controversy over ECINet, the ECI’s integrated digital platform for electoral processes. The Indian Express reported concerns raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over the centralisation of electoral-roll databases and access available to state-level officials.The ECI has maintained that ECINet is decentralised and that statutory responsibilities remain with designated election officials.On September 26, the poll panel also formed a committee, headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner and including an independent IIT or IIIT expert, to review ECINet’s compliance with laws and rules.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to an early listing of a plea challenging the manner in which the Election Commission of India (ECI) is functioning. The plea comes amid controversy over ECINet, the ECI’s integrated digital platform for electoral processes.

Article Title: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 cr of 12.10 cr
Article Text:
AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 crore

How other regional parties fared

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party received Rs 12.10 crore in contributions in 2025-26, a 68% drop from the previous financial year, according to its latest report filed with the Election Commission.Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Both gave Rs 5 crore each. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta.The remaining contributions amounted to around Rs 2.10 crore, according to the report.Gupta was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an AAP ticket in October 2025. Trident's Rs 5-crore cheque was dated January 9, 2026, when Gupta was still with the AAP.He joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion, merging two-third of AAP's Rajya Sabha strength into the ruling saffron party in April this year.The AAP had reported contributions of Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25, compared with Rs 11.06 crore in 2023-24. Prudent Electoral Trust was the party's biggest donor that year, contributing Rs 16.40 crore.The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025.The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based.The AAP report has 1,202 numbered entries. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora is listed against 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each, adding up to Rs 1.20 lakh.The latest filings of other regional parties also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25.The Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which came to power in Andhra Pradesh, reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year. Prudent Electoral Trust was its biggest donor, giving Rs 45 crore, compared with Rs 40 crore in 2024-25.The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which lost power in Andhra Pradesh to the TDP, reported contributions of Rs 24.31 crore. This was sharply lower than the Rs 140.04 crore it reported in 2024-25. Its biggest donor in the latest filing was Goodwood Sanctuary Private Limited, which contributed Rs 10 crore.The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), which lost power in Odisha in 2024, did not report any contribution above Rs 20,000 in its latest filing. The party had reported Rs 60 crore in 2024-25, all of it received in April and May 2024, before the election results.The BJD had also reported no such contributions in 2022-23 and 2023-24, when electoral bonds were still available.Under the rules, political parties have to disclose the names of donors who contribute more than Rs 20,000 in a financial year.However, these contribution reports do not represent a party's total annual income, which is disclosed separately in its audited accounts.
Article Summary: Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta. Gupta joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion.

Article Title: Dhaka begins search for missing Assam woman
Article Text:
The Gauhati High Court

NEW DELHI:

Tribunal declared Assam woman a foreigner, but Gauhati HC set it aside

Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum, who was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India on the case.Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, additional secretary (Political and Immigration), Bangladesh home ministry, whose office deals with border enforcement, illegal crossings and cross-border deportations, said officials were trying to locate Mumtaz but had no information as of Sunday. The matter was sent to police and other depts late on Sept 27, days after TOI reached out.Gauhati HC on Sept 3 directed MEA to "endeavour to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back". The HC also directed Assam govt to pay her husband Mujammel Hoque Rs 2 lakh interim compensation, observing "she was expelled without her husband or an adult family member being informed". HC found it denied her a chance to challenge it, a violation of democratic due process.Underscoring that basic human rights extend to anyone on Indian soil, the bench directed Assam Police and home dept to "ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed about tribunal orders and that their adult family members are notified before they are moved outside their district".The court criticised the tribunal for stripping her of the "opportunity to challenge the Foreigners Tribunal's opinion before Gauhati HC".With no information in India, TOI contacted journalists, human-rights activists, officials and govt and security establishment sources across Bangladesh, focusing on Sylhet division and adjoining districts, where she could have ended up.A senior Dhaka-based businessman, who wishes to stay anonymous, joined authorities in the search and is working with govt and security contacts. An appeal with her photo and identification details, including Foreigners Identification Portal ID, was published in prominent Bengali newspapers on Sept 22. Bangla daily Manob Kantha also carried her photo and reported on the family's search.Official efforts in Sylhet, however, have found no lead. Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sarwar Murshed Shamim said police had "tried to locate Mumtaz within the metropolitan area but had not found her and were continuing the search."Mumtaz, from Nagaon, was declared a foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal. The HC set aside the opinion and ordered fresh consideration, finding deficiencies in its assessment of evidence including 1965 and 1970 voter-list records of her grandfather, her father's 1977 voter-list record and voter ID, Gaonburah and Gaon Panchayat certificates, a school transfer certificate and land records.She appeared before the tribunal on May 30 with her lawyer, after which police took her into custody. She was taken to Juria and Nagaon Sadar police stations, Matia holding centre in Goalpara, then Eraligool holding centre in Sribhumi (June 4-13).Handed to BSF on June 13, she was sent to Bangladesh on June 14 from Kalaincherra, Cachar, BSF told the HC. Three months on, police, authorities and civil-society members are trying to establish where she is.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum. She was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India.

Article Title: Rape cases peaked at 2,199 in 2015, dropped to 1,901 in '25
Article Text: Changes in the law after the Nirbhaya case , which made registration of FIRs mandatory in offences against women, saw rape cases rise from 1,636 in 2013 to 2,166 in 2014 and peak at 2,199 in 2015. Cases fell to 1,699 in 2020 (due to Covid lockdown), the lowest level since 2013 at that point. The number crossed the 2,000-mark again in 2021 and reached 2,141 in 2023. A decline followed, with cases dropping from 2,141 in 2023 to 2,076 in 2024 and further to 1,901 in 2025.

Article Title: Jails are hiring grounds for pro-Khalistan groups; dead drops of ISI modules also under intel lens
Article Text:
Khalistan groups target north India jails to recruit operatives, agencies flag growing threat

NEW DELHI: Intelligence agencies have flagged attempts by pro-Khalistan groups, including Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), to infiltrate jails in north India and recruit operatives. The move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's contact while serving time in Patiala jail.Agencies are now investigating the digital footprint, dead-drop financial channels, and the broader jail recruitment network, sources said. Agencies have also noted how ISI-backed modules are increasingly relying on dead-drop methods to channel funds, supply weapons, and execute covert tasks and have largely replaced physical handovers with pre-designated drop points along isolated highway stretches and border and rural sectors.Drawn straight from the classic spycraft playbook, this method ensures that foreign masterminds or handlers remain completely insulated from the foot soldiers executing their commands on the ground. Arms, ammunition, and untraceable cash, frequently delivered across the border via drones or covert couriers, are hidden at specific coordinates, with retrieval instructions transmitted to local operatives over end-to-end encrypted messaging platforms like Signal.The tactic of leveraging prison networks draws from a pattern highlighted by high-profile incidents like the 2016 Nabha jailbreak, which exposed the nexus between terror outfits and incarcerated criminal groups. Within these facilities, handlers and radicalised inmates target vulnerable, economically distressed prisoners - frequently first-time offenders or petty criminals lacking legal representation and financial support.In the latest instance, agencies recently busted an SFJ-backed module and arrested operative Preetpal Singh, who, along with his associates, had spray-painted anti-Brics and pro-Khalistan graffiti across Delhi and Punjab, filmed the act and sent the video to Pannun. Singh, it turned out, had a prior history of pro-Khalistan activities, having been arrested in 2023 for a similar crime.While in prison, he was provided with a phone number to contact Pannun and execute future tasks. After his release in 2026, Singh established direct contact with Pannun and received Rs 1.5 lakh through a dead-drop location on the Faridkot-Amritsar highway. Preetpal subsequently recruited another inmate, also on bail, for the Delhi assignment.
Article Summary: Intelligence agencies have flagged attempts by pro-Khalistan groups to infiltrate jails in north India and recruit operatives. Move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's contact while serving time in Patiala jail.

Article Title: H1N1 dominates flu strains in India, accounts for 3 out of 4 cases: WHO
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: H1N1 is the dominant flu strain detected in India, accounting for three out of every four influenza-positive samples reported in the latest surveillance data, according to World Health Organization (WHO).The finding is from WHO's surveillance data for weeks 36 and 37 of 2026, covering Sept 1 to 14 and updated on Sept 21. Across the South-East Asia region, 817 of 3,632 samples tested positive for influenza, giving an overall positivity rate of 22%.India stood out for a high share of H1N1 among its positive samples. The A(H1N1)pdm09 accounted for 75% of influenza-positive samples in India, compared with 50% across the region. It was also the dominant strain in Bhutan and Thailand, where it accounted for 97% and74% respectively.Dr Rommel Tickoo, senior director, internal medicine, Max hospital, said H1N1 remains a seasonal strain, with higher complication risks for older adults, pregnant women, young children and people with underlying illnesses. He advised vaccination, respiratory hygiene, early testing where appropriate and timely antiviral treatment for high-risk patients.
Article Summary: H1N1 is the dominant flu strain detected in India. It accounts for three out of every four influenza-positive samples reported. Across the South-East Asia region, 817 of 3,632 samples tested positive for influenza, giving an overall positivity rate of 22%.

Article Title: US waives tariff on speciality drugs imported from India
Article Text:
US exempts speciality drugs from tariffs on imports from India, 19 countries

The US will not charge any ad valorem tariff on certain speciality drugs and associated ingredients used for treatment of rare medical conditions imported from India and 19 other countries.The US commerce department published the list of countries in the Federal Register as it prepares to impose a 100% tariff on certain patented pharmaceutical imports and associated ingredients from Sept 29.On Apr 2, President Trump issued a proclamation to impose tariffs on imports of patented pharmaceuticals, biologics and associated ingredients into US as part of efforts to encourage domestic production.Eligible products for the zero per cent tariff rate include drugs designated for rare diseases, infertility treatments, cell therapies, gene therapies, antibody-drug conjugates and animal pharmaceuticals. Components of these drugs are subject to a zero per cent tariff rate.Generic pharma products and associated ingredients are not subject to Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs, according to the commerce dept notice.
Article Summary: The US will not charge any ad valorem tariff on certain speciality drugs and associated ingredients used for treatment of rare medical conditions imported from India and 19 other countries. The US commerce department published the list of countries in the Federal Register as it prepares to impose a 100% tariff.

Article Title: Explain legal basis of MDR, Supreme Court tells Centre
Article Text:
Supreme Court questions UPI MDR, asks Centre, RBI to explain legal basis

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday asked the Centre, RBI and National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to explain under which provision of law the merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions was imposed, even though it refused to stay its implementation from Oct 15."Is it a tax or a fee? If it is not a tax or a fee, then what is the executive scope of making this expropriation on transactions? What is the character of this expropriation?" asked a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing a PIL that argued that MDR charges on UPI transactions would make people revert to cash dealings, which would encourage accumulation of black money.Additional solicitor general N Venkataraman (ASG) said MDR is not a tax or a fee, nor an expropriation as govt will not get even a paisa from it. It is akin to service charges levied by banks on transactions done earlier through credit and debit cards, though MDR's scope is much more restricted. He said that 96% of the transactions are exempted from MDR, while from within the balance 4%, essential services will attract a flat charge of Rs 5. For the rest, transactions above Rs 75,000 will attract a maximum MDR of Rs 300. Justice Bagchi asked, "What is this service charge? Please file an affidavit and explain.It cannot be through executive fiat."Explaining the operation of credit and debit cards, the predecessors of the UPI mode of transferring money, and the service charge attached to such transactions because of the involvement of banks and the aggregator, Venkatraman said there is no difference between UPI and the previous system, and it involves a service charge payable to banks and aggregator NPCI, which facilitates the transactions. "Govt does not take a rupee from it," he said.Justice Bagchi said, "When it is a charge in terms of provisions of the Income Tax Act, on whose hand is it an income?" Venkatraman said the provision of the Income Tax Act cited by the court is an enabling provision which recognises UPI money transfers as a valid transaction, nothing more, nothing less.When the bench asked who takes the MDR amount, the Centre said it will be the banks and the aggregator, like for credit or debit cards. It has nothing to do with law as it is purely an administrative mechanism, the ASG said.CJI Kant said, "It appears more technical than law. It would be better if the govt, RBI and NPCI file their affidavits explaining the entire issue." Referring to full-page advertisements in Monday newspapers explaining the MDR, the CJI said, "We have read your advance arguments in the newspapers. Yet, you file a detailed affidavit." The petitioner's counsel sought a stay on the imposition of MDR, a plea Venkatraman opposed, saying it will come into force on Oct 15. The bench brushed aside the plea for a stay and asked the Centre, RBI and NPCI to file affidavits in four weeks.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks Centre, RBI to explain legal basis for merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions. Solicitor general says MDR is not a tax or a fee, nor an expropriation as govt will not get even a paisa from it.

NEW DELHI: Agreeing with Supreme Court, Centre on Monday said it would soon insert a provision in the Information and Technology Intermediary Rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing children under 18 years of age to open social media accounts, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.Agreeing with the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana as well as petitioner NGO 'Just Rights for Children Alliance' counsel H S Phoolka, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the agreements entered into by intermediaries and minors were void contracts and these must be prevented.Membership of educational websites can be taken through consent of parents," solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, adding that Centre would step in to make it a statutory obligation for intermediaries not to allow minors to have social media accounts.Justice Bagchi said, "They have registered under the laws of US and imported into Indian digital space the restrictions which are applicable in US (on minors' opening accounts on social media platforms), which is impermissible under Indian law."When Mehta said "we will have to control intermediaries", the bench responded, "Our request to you - will Centre pass some directions under Intermediary Rules that they should fashion their software or platform in conformity with Indian laws?"The SG said, "They will have to conform to Indian laws and there is no doubt about it.Something can be done, something should be done and something will be done." Article Title: FBI puts gangster Goldy Brar on Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list
Article Text:
Goldy Brar enters FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list as manhunt goes global

NEW DELHI: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has officially placed notorious gangster Satinderjeet Singh aka Goldy Brar, on its famed Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.The announcement, made early Tuesday, by the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, marks a major escalation in international law enforcement efforts targeting transnational crime syndicates operating across North America and Asia.Brar, who becomes the 543rd fugitive added to the historic list, faces multiple federal indictments in the United States, including Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) conspiracy, extortion, and narcotics trafficking.According to federal prosecutors, the fugitive serves as the primary North American operational leader for the Lawrence Bishnoi Organized Crime Group. Operating from a prison cell in India via contraband communications, Bishnoi allegedly delegated international operations to trusted lieutenants like Brar.The syndicate has been linked to a trail of violence across North America, including targeted assassinations, kidnappings, armed extortions, and large-scale drug smuggling—including the theft of over 500 kilograms of cocaine from rival cartels in the Los Angeles region.Among the most high-profile offenses detailed in federal court documents is the June 2023 assassination of prominent political and religious figure "H.S.N." outside a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia.Bishnoi and Brar are charged with ordering the targeted killing. Canadian authorities subsequently designated the Bishnoi syndicate as a terrorist entity in September 2025, highlighting its routine use of public violence and social media threat campaigns to extort individuals within Indian diaspora communities worldwide.Brar’s inclusion on the Top Ten list stems from "Operation Hardball," a years-long multi-agency investigation that unsealed indictments against 37 defendants connected to India-based transnational crime groups in July 2026. While 28 defendants have been taken into custody or located, five key fugitives remain at large alongside Brar.Law enforcement leaders from the FBI, the Los Angeles Police Department, and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) emphasized that placing Brar on the global list ensures his face will be publicized worldwide until he is captured.Considered armed, extremely violent, and dangerous, Brar is believed to be hiding in parts of California or Canada. Authorities advise the public to avoid direct interaction and to submit tips directly to the FBI.
Article Summary: FBI places notorious gangster Satinderjeet Singh aka Goldy Brar on its famed Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. Article Title: Government deploys AI tool to scrutinise rural road project DPRs

NEW DELHI: In a bid to cut down delays and improve quality, the government has deployed an AI-based detailed project report (DPR) scrutiny tool that aims at strengthening and streamlining the technical appraisal of rural road projects under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana.Rolled out by rural development ministry’s National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency, last week, the tool, Parakh, has been implemented on a pilot basis in all states and UTs to assess its applicability and effectiveness. DPR preparation is a critical stage in rural road development, involving assessment of alignment, geometry, pavement design, traffic, soil and subgrade conditions, drainage, cross-drainage structures, quantities and cost estimates.With thousands of DPRs requiring multi-level technical scrutiny, the govt is hoping that this AI-enabled tool will substantially reduce repetitive scrutiny time, identify deficiencies at an early stage and facilitate faster processing of DPRs, thereby accelerating sanction, execution and timely completion of PMGSY works.As of now the same parameters are often checked repeatedly at different scrutiny levels, resulting in duplication of effort and longer processing time.Consequently, sanction of works gets delayed, affecting subsequent execution and completion.Rural development secretary Rohit Kansal said, “Transparent and consistent technical scrutiny is essential for better planning and timely implementation of PMGSY projects. Through Parakh, AI is being used to make the scrutiny of DPRs simpler, more systematic and more evidence-based.”“This will help technical experts identify key areas requiring attention and focus more on complex cases. At the same time, it will make the technical evaluation process more effective and transparent, further strengthening the quality of rural road projects,” he added.Since the scale of the rural road projects involved is vast — around 63,914 km of road length completed in past four years, inlcuding the ongoing fiscal year — officials said Parakh is designed to assist technical experts by using Al to analyse DPR data, undertake standardised checks and flag inconsistencies in the DPR during the scrutiny process.
Article Summary: The tool, Parakh, has been implemented on a pilot basis in all states and UTs. It aims at strengthening and streamlining the technical appraisal of rural road projects under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. The same parameters are often checked repeatedly at different scrutiny levels.

Article Title: UNFPA report: Migrant workers cite livelihood insecurity, low wages, poverty and debt as reasons for moving out for better life

For migrant workers, moving brings better livelihoods—but little job security

NEW DELHI: Nearly 72% of migrant workers surveyed in three south Indian states felt that moving for work has improved their standard of living and more than half (around 57%) intended to continue working in their destination state, as per a new report.At the same time, it turns out that over 86% of workers have no signed employment contracts and many face difficulties ranging from accessing welfare and essential services to experiencing language, communication and social barriers.Clearly migration decisions are shaped strongly by livelihood insecurity and limited employment opportunities. Migrants cited low wages at origin, lack of jobs, better opportunities, irregular employment, poverty and debt among the principal reasons for moving.These findings are part of the South India Interstate Migration Survey (SIIMS) 2026, that offers first-of-its-kind data on the changing nature of migration within India and on how migrant workers from other states (primarily from northern and eastern) live and work in Karnataka, Keralam and Tamil Nadu.The study surveyed 1,824 migrant workers and covered sectors including agriculture, fishing and marine work, and daily labour in all three states.It also covered hospitality in Keralam, textile and garment work in Tamil Nadu, and scrap collection in Karnataka.Over 92% of the migrants came from West Bengal (26.2%), Bihar (21.8%), Assam (17.1%), Odisha (12%), UP (9.6%) and Jharkhand (5.6%).Conducted by the International Institute of Migration and Development (IIMAD), the study was supported by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM).It comes through that over 77% of the surveyed workers were recruited through non-contractor channels, nearly 58% are paid in cash with Rs 17640 the average monthly wage and the average working day being 9.87 hours. The report also brings into focus the gender disparity as it came through that women workers earned about Rs 3,313 less per month than men.The data shows that just a little over 19% of migrant workers can easily use their welfare benefits when they move between states; 35% can do so partly and around 45% can barely do so.It also comes through that over 73% face problems accessing welfare and 69% face problems accessing healthcare.The survey found that while 88.2% of migrant workers are included in formal financial services, exclusion was higher in Karnataka (26.8%) and among scrap collection workers (31.3%).The study recommends building on One Nation One Ration Card so that welfare benefits follow the worker, multilingual help desks and helplines, stronger labour inspection and closer coordination between states.Andrea M Wojnar, UNFPA India Representative and Country Director Bhutan said, “By highlighting critical gaps in welfare portability, healthcare access, and workplace protections, this study provides a clear roadmap for stakeholders to turn data into targeted action.”
Article Summary: Nearly 72% of migrant workers surveyed in three south Indian states felt that moving for work has improved their standard of living. Article Title: Indian imports of Russian crude oil to decline further amid lower exports, Chinese competition

NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to decline further in October and November, owing to lower exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the country to buy costlier alternatives for the rest of the year.People familiar with procurement plans told Reuters that some Indian refiners would not receive adequate Russian supplies in October and November."Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners," a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said.According to analytics firm Kpler, Russian oil arrivals in India are set to drop to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest level since April.Trade data showed that arrivals had already fallen 16.5 per cent to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, although Russia remained India's main supplier, ahead of the UAE and Venezuela.Overall availability of Russian exports has reportedly shrunk, particularly from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have roughly halved as repeated drone attacks have suspended loadings.India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts.In recent months, however, China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as Middle Eastern supplies tightened because of the Iran war.Traders told Reuters that refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia's Urals grade, while also buying Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes.Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows to China.Seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) offers a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China, whereas shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis."It's not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination," another trader told Reuters, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.
Article Summary: India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022. China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as Middle Eastern supplies tighten. Russian oil arrivals in India are set to drop to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest level since April.

NEW DELHI: India and France are preparing to launch 'Trishna' from Sriharikota in 2027 to monitor energy and water budgets of the Earth. The earth observation satellite 'Trishna' (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment), a collaborative endeavour between Isro and French space agency CNES, is engineered to deliver high spatial and high temporal resolution monitoring of Earth's surface temperature, emissivity, biophysical and radiation variables for surface energy budgeting at regional to global scale.While meeting a big French delegation related to cooperation in the space and science sector, space and science minister Jitendra Singh said the realisation of the “joint satellite, TRISHNA, is progressing well, and also appreciated CNES support to India's Gaganyaan programme, including supply of consumables and training of flight surgeons”. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.The 'Trishna' mission will also help in a comprehensive assessment of urban heat islands, detection of thermal anomalies linked to volcanic activity and geothermal resources, and precise monitoring of snow-melt runoff and glacier dynamics. The mission will also provide valuable data on aerosol optical depth, atmospheric water vapor, and cloud cover.A high-level French delegation led by Philippe Baptiste, French minister for higher education, research and space, met Singh in Delhi on Monday and they talked about the Space Summit, India-France Year of Innovation 2026 and priorities in scientific and technological cooperation, including space, CEFIPRA and blue economy.Singh said India-France space cooperation has evolved from the early sounding rocket experiments of the 1960s into a broad and expanding partnership encompassing joint satellite missions, launch vehicle technologies, human spaceflight and emerging space applications. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.Referring to India’s space-sector reforms and the growth of the private ecosystem, he said over 400 Indian space startups are now engaged in areas, including rocket building, satellite building and space applications. He said the next phase of India-France cooperation can bring together government institutions, industries and start-ups on both sides to create a larger ecosystem and wider resource pool.Philippe Baptiste described 'Trishna' as a strong example of what India and France can achieve together, and welcomed greater cooperation in human spaceflight, astronaut health, microgravity research and parabolic flights.
Article Summary: India and France are preparing to launch 'Trishna' from Sriharikota in 2027 to monitor energy and water budgets of the Earth. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday suggested recovering unpaid traffic e-challans by linking them to electricity bills, after noting a massive Rs 20,000 crore outstanding balance.While hearing a plea, the bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan was told that, although a vast number of traffic challans are being issued, the recovery of fines remains minimal.The top court was informed that states and UTs had around Rs 45,000 crore outstanding in e-challans, of which approximately Rs 25,000 crore has been recovered so far.The court said that simply continuing to issue e-challans is not enough, and that recovering the fines is just as important."If people are not paying traffic challans, add it to their electricity dues bill. Article Title: Centre discusses drought measures to protect Rabi crops in the country
Article Text:
Centre discusses drought measures to protect Rabi crops in the country

NEW DELHI: Apprehending a threat of deficient monsoon rainfall to the upcoming sowing season, Centre on Monday discussed contingency measures to minimise its impact on Rabi (winter-sown) crops, with Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan calling for data-driven planning, stronger centre-state coordination, weekly crop monitoring, balanced fertiliser use and water budgeting.Amid indications that the kharif (summer-sown) crops’ output may not match last year’s level despite progress in acreage, the minister, while addressing farm scientists and policymakers during a national conference, also emphasised the need to drive the Rabi strategy through less water-consuming pulses and oilseeds. The latest acreage data shows the total sown area at 1,107 lakh hectares (ha) as of Friday was about three lakh ha more than the ‘normal’ (average of last five years) acreage (1,104 lakh ha) despite a cumulative deficit of 12% in monsoon rainfall in the country. It was, however, 14 lakh ha less than the same period of 2025, a year which recorded 8% more than normal rainfall.The conference was convened to discuss the farm strategy, keeping in view the current drought situation in many states, so that the impact of low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation due to deficient rainfall may not impact farming operations much. Sowing of rabi crops such as wheat and mustard begins in October.The Centre will, meanwhile, send teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation. Nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected and the state has already declared a drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions due to the monsoon rainfall deficit of 30%.The monsoon season will end on Wednesday with a strong possibility of an overall rainfall deficit of more than 10% in the country as a whole — a deficient condition which is considered a drought. As of Monday, India recorded a deficit of 12% in cumulative (June 1–Sept 28) monsoon rainfall, with 12 states reporting a deficit of 20% or more.Underlining the current situation, Chouhan asked every district to assess the water available for irrigation before finalising crop plans. “Areas with limited water availability should prioritise less water-intensive crops such as pulses and oilseeds, while areas with assured irrigation can plan other crops accordingly,” he said while noting that the rainfed areas, in particular, require careful planning as the availability of soil moisture largely determines the crop choice and outcome.Rabi crops are normally sown in a total area of about 638 lakh hectares, out of which wheat generally covers nearly 50% of it, with the remaining around 50% being covered by pulses, oilseeds and coarse cereals.
Article Summary: Centre on Monday discussed contingency measures to minimise its impact on Rabi (winter-sown) crops. Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called for data-driven planning, stronger centre-state coordination, weekly crop monitoring, balanced fertiliser use and water budgeting.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom.
